page: Amazon Web Services m3.medium is a general-purpose, third-generation virtual machine instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 4 GB NVMe SSD. It does not include any GPU hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and its baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the m3.medium sits in the lower performance tiers. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng at 1259.98, falls into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 11.78 GB/sec and write speeds at 10.36 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10%. Cryptographic and compression tasks show weak to poor results, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 484.21 and single-threaded gzip compression at 21.46 GB/sec.

Given its legacy hardware profile and low resource density, the m3.medium presents significant performance tradeoffs. It is not configured for modern compute-heavy or memory-intensive tasks, as demonstrated by its low Geekbench multi-core score of 669.0 and static web serving throughput of 1.47 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a low-cost entry point for legacy workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable models, but it offers low performance per resource. Appropriate workloads are limited to lightweight utility services, basic testing, or low-traffic static web serving.
